messages:
Julian: Heads up — EU audit next week asked for our consent routing matrix and a concrete backstop playbook if an EU primary becomes unreachable. Can we finalize today?
Tara: Thanks for the ping. I sketched a compact consent matrix earlier, but need agreement on safe fallbacks. Short version: 1) strict residency -> refuse fallback, 2) consent-permitted -> fallback to nearest EU region, 3) anonymized-mode allowed -> degrade to pseudonymized embeddings in-host.
Sam: Quick Q: how do we handle KV cache ownership when we fallback? We can't risk serving stale PII from an out-of-region cache.
Tara: Right — rule: cache entries labelled residency=EU must be invalidated on cross-region fallback. TTL reduction + eviction + write-through to primary when available.
Julian: Proposed backstop playbook (concise):
- Detect (5m): heartbeats show EU primary unreachable + >1 downstream retry
- Quarantine (0-2m): mark incoming EU-resident requests as QUARANTINE (respond 429/hold) while we evaluate
- Policy decision (manual or auto): check consent flag for tenant -> route or degrade
- Route (fast path): if consented, route to EU secondary; if not consent but anonymization allowed, switch to anonymized-mode; else return controlled error with remediation steps
- Cache hygiene: purge residency-tagged caches and mark future writes with residency-origin header
- Rollback: once EU heartbeats normal for 10m and KV sync validated -> lift quarantine
Sam: Can we make the manual step optional? For high-severity outages we need automatic safe-path to keep SLA. Maybe allow auto-degrade only if traffic pattern and audit flags clear.
Tara: Agree. Add a precedence table: auto-degrade allowed only if tenant-level policy = AUTO_DEGRADE_ACCEPTED AND legal-override false. Otherwise require ops ack.
Julian: Example routing policy pseudocode: ```
if primary_unreachable and tenant.policy.auto_degrade:
  if tenant.consent == "EU" then route("eu-secondary")
  elif tenant.consent == "ANON_OK" then set_mode("pseudonymize")
  else return 451, "Regionally restricted: contact support"
else return 503
```
Sam: About KMS/HSM — when we switch to pseudonymized embeddings, keys must be different (no recoverable PII). Ops, please ensure we rotate or use derived-key path for anonymization. Otherwise legal will complain.
Tara: Noted. We'll use a derived context key for anonymized-mode and log key-id in audit trails.
Julian: Testing plan:
- Sim S1: kill EU primary, run 10k EU requests, assert no PII leaves region unless consented
- Sim S2: fail KV read and check cache purge path and write-through fallback
- Sim S3: verify rollback path and no double-write anomalies
Sam: I'll wire up the chaos test harness and a validation script to scan outputs for PII artifacts (regex-based). ETA tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Tara: Also need documentation for support: canned messages, how to surface tenant consent flags, steps to rekey KMS if required. I'll draft.
Julian: One more edgecase — cross-tenant models: if a model pool is shared across regions, we need model-containment flags so EU-only models don't get served by global replicas. Add model residency metadata and strict deny in the router for EU-only models.
Sam: Good call. I'll add a router check: reject serve if model.residency == EU_ONLY and target_region != eu.
eng-arch-bot: Summary saved to /playbooks/consent-backstop-v1.md and linked to runbook. CI job "consent-backstop-check" will run S1-S3 on the next deploy.
Tara: OK let's merge this as v1. Julian, Sam — can you PR the playbook + tests? I'll review and then we'll present to legal ops tomorrow.
Julian: PR incoming in 30m. Thanks everyone.
Sam: On it. Will tag you both when tests pass.
eng-arch-bot: Deploy scheduling note: blocked on downstream KMS changes (ticket #INF-872).
Tara: Filed KMS ticket and pinged security. We'll update status in the doc. :white_check_mark:
